E3.text: You tend to run a mechanism backwards, placing the stone or the severity where the familiar picture puts it. Narrate cause first: where does the stone sit, what does it press on, what does ischaemia do.

E4.text: You tend to stretch a general risk to every case, here stone means surgery. Ask what the actual yearly risk is and which named feature turns a silent stone into an indication.

E5.text: You tend to answer from one source, either the remembered past-paper key or the modern text. For key conflicts, hold both as a pair: the old key and current practice.
